Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the StratoCloud Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by one. There will be a brief pause while we poll for questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing StratoCloud's results for the Q2 2024. With me on the call are David Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Mark Thompson, Chief Product Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Sales Officer; and Tom Reilly, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to David Harlan.

David Harlan:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. StratoCloud continued its strong growth trajectory in Q2, driven by robust demand for our comprehensive suite of cloud services and solutions.

During the quarter, our key priorities included expanding our presence in emerging markets, accelerating the adoption of our AI-powered platform, enhancing our developer ecosystem, strengthening our commitment to sustainability, investing in employee training and development, improving cross-functional collaboration, and ensuring the security and privacy of our customers' data.

As we wrap up a transformative Q2, let me highlight our key achievements that propelled us forward in this hyper-growth phase of the cloud computing landscape. Our results reflect the relentless demand for scalable, secure, and AI-infused infrastructure, aligning with Gartner's projection of global cloud spend surpassing $700 billion by 2025 at a 20% CAGR for public cloud services.

Starting with the standout numbers: Q2 revenue reached $8.7 billion, up 32% year-over-year and 8% sequentially, beating our guidance and consensus. Annual Recurring Revenue, or ARR, climbed 28% to $36.2 billion, with net new ARR of $2.4 billion—our best quarter on record. Remaining Performance Obligations, or RPO, jumped 45% to $52 billion, providing a strong multi-year backlog from customer migrations.

Customer-wise, we added 4,200 net new customers, totaling 52,000, including 1,200 in the $1 million-plus ARR tier. Dollar-based net retention reached 118%, powered by expansions in high-margin areas like our StratoAI platform. We closed 15 deals over $100 million in total contract value, highlighted by a $250 million, five-year pact with a Fortune 10 retailer for mainframe-to-cloud migration using StratoCore IaaS and StratoDB services, expecting 3x consumption growth in year one.

AI and machine learning workloads exploded, now 42% of net new bookings, up from 28% last year. Our NVIDIA DGX Cloud with H100 and Blackwell GPUs handled over 15 exaFLOPS of AI training, aiding a top pharma in speeding drug discovery by 40%. StratoAI serverless inference grew 150% YoY, with sub-100ms latency for generative AI apps.

Geographically, Americas at 58% of revenue grew 35% YoY, capitalizing on enterprise shifts from AWS and Azure. EMEA rose 29%, boosted by GDPR-compliant sovereign clouds and government wins in Frankfurt and Paris. APAC surged 42%, with Mumbai and Singapore data centers at 95% utilization for 5G edge and telco IoT.

Operationally, non-GAAP operating margin hit 32%, up 400 basis points, thanks to StratoX1 ARM instances powering 25% of workloads at 30% lower TCO. Free cash flow was $2.1 billion, or 24% of revenue, supporting $15 billion in 2024 capex for AI. Sustainability advanced with 100% renewable matching globally and StratoGreen tool adoption by 20% of enterprises, cutting Scope 2 emissions 28%.

Moving to strategic priorities for the AI-first, multi-cloud era, we're targeting the $200 billion AI cloud market by 2027. First, AI ubiquity via $5 billion FY24 investment for 500 MW GPU capacity, StratoForge open-source MLOps with 50,000 downloads, and partnerships with Hugging Face and Meta for Llama 3, aiming for 50%+ AI revenue growth and 30% of ARR by FY25.

Second, sovereign and edge expansion with five new zones in Mexico City, Riyadh, Jakarta, Warsaw, and Sydney for FedRAMP and IRAP equivalents; StratoEdge 2.0 for <10ms 5G latency, winning automotive simulations.

Third, multi-cloud mastery through StratoLink federating AWS Outposts and Azure Stack, 25% attach rates cutting egress 60%, plus Snowflake and Databricks integrations for 40% H2 analytics growth.

Fourth, security with zero-trust StratoShield blocking 2.5 trillion threats, pioneering post-quantum crypto for financial clients at 22% of revenue.

Fifth, operational excellence and talent, hiring 5,000 engineers including AI PhDs, expanding in Bangalore and Toronto to hit 25-30% FY24 growth ($36-37 billion revenue) and 35% margins.

These achievements validate our flywheel of innovation, enterprise wins, global expansion, and value delivery. We've raised FY24 guidance to $35.8-36.2 billion revenue and $14.5-15 billion non-GAAP operating income.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, David. We are pleased to report another quarter of strong financial results. Revenue grew by 32% year-over-year to $8.7 billion, exceeding our guidance. Our gross margin was 71.2%, reflecting our efficient cost structure. Our operating margin was 32%.

Before moving on, let me elaborate on our overall gross margin trends and drivers, a key area of interest. We're seeing sustained strength from platform maturity and strategic shifts in this competitive hyperscale market.

Headline: Gross margin expanded 210 basis points YoY to 71.2%, from 69.1% last year and up from 70.4% in Q1—our eighth straight quarter of expansion, matching AWS at 71% and topping Azure's 69%. Trailing twelve months at 70.5%, enabling leverage as revenue scales.

Key positives: First, product mix. Higher-margin AI/ML via ForgeML—our foundation models and inference like AWS Bedrock—grew 45% YoY to 28% of revenue at 80%+ margins from software economics on custom silicon. PaaS/SaaS analytics like data lakehouse rivaling Snowflake/Databricks hit 35% mix at 75-78% margins. IaaS at 37% revenue, 22% growth, but 62-65% margins. Mix shift added ~150 bps.

Second, scale efficiencies across 42 regions, 120+ zones. Next-gen data centers 60% on ForgeCore ASICs cut inference costs 35%, power efficiency up 28% with PUE <1.15 liquid cooling. ARM Graviton-like CPUs for 40% workloads saved 20% vs x86. Fiber expansions cut egress 15%, plus DRAM/NAND deals added 100 bps.

Regionally: North America (52% revenue) at 73.5% from high-ARPU enterprise sovereign clouds. EMEA (28%) 70.8%, GDPR AI tailwinds offset energy costs. APAC (15%, 38% growth) 67.2% from pricing vs Alibaba/Tencent and edge investments. LatAm/India ~65%, prioritizing volume; RPO $145B up 32%.

Headwinds: 60 bps from SMB mix, free tiers; 20 bps USD strength vs JPY/INR; AI capex $12B pressured utilization to 85%.

Forward: Q3 71.5-72.0%, expanding FY25 with AI mix to 35%, sustainability renewables, CloudForge One TCO savings 30%.

This sets us up strongly amid industry $200B+ AI capex.

Next, I'd like to introduce Elena Vasquez, who will provide an update on our technology roadmap.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. We are making significant investments in research and development to stay at the forefront of cloud innovation. We are particularly excited about our progress in AI-powered platforms across global regions.

Let me provide an update on our geographic revenue breakdown and trends, which highlight the strength and diversification of our tech deployments. In Q2, total revenue was $8.7 billion, up 32% YoY, powered by IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, and AI boom. For FY24 to date, Americas 56% or ~$20 billion annualized, EMEA 24%, APAC 20%; Q2 mix shifted to Americas 55% ($4.8B), EMEA 24% ($2.1B), APAC 21% ($1.8B). International now 45%, up from 39% two years ago.

In Americas, $4.8B up 22% YoY/8% QoQ, U.S. 92% ($4.4B) from AI/ML surge 35%, e.g., financial giant migrating H100s to Phoenix/Virginia; RPO $185B up 42%. Canada/LatAm $0.4B up 18%, Brazil investments for sovereign. AetherEdge CDN cuts transfer 25%; margins 72% despite GCP pressure.

EMEA $2.1B up 32% amid macro softness; UK/Germany 45% ($0.95B), Frankfurt/London expansions for 28% PaaS share. AI sovereignty grew 45%, e.g., €1.2B UK G-Cloud for NIS2 enclaves. Middle East $0.35B up 55% Vision 2030; Africa doubles to $0.15B telco 5G. Renewables PUE 1.15 beats Azure.

APAC shone at $1.8B, 42% YoY/12% QoQ; Japan/Australia 38% ($0.7B), Tokyo Kubernetes for SoftBank AI. India $0.4B 65% growth UPI fintech; SE Asia $0.35B 50% Singapore hub; China $0.15B partnered. Edge 60% IoT growth; RPO $95B up 55%, 20k Blackwell GPUs.

Trends: AI 32% revenue up from 18%, open K8s/eBPF portability. FY25 $18B capex 40% international: sovereign in 12 countries, AI regions, PUE 1.12, carbon-neutral 2030. International up 38% vs 20% domestic; FY25 $115-120B revenue, APAC to 25% mix.

Now, I'll pass it to Mark Thompson for a product update.

Mark Thompson:
Thank you, Elena. We recently launched ForgeML, which is already gaining significant traction in the market.

Today, I'd like to focus on our customer churn rate and retention trends, core to our product's stickiness in cloud. Our gross dollar retention was 92% in Q2, up from 91% Q1 and 300 bps better than 89% Q2 2023—quarterly dollar churn at 2.4%, lowest in two years. Enterprise (> $1M ARR, 68%) at 1.8% down from 2.6%; SMBs 4.1% improved via self-service.

Net revenue retention (NRR) at 118%, beating AWS 114%/GCP 112%, with 42% base expanding on AetherAI and containers.

Drivers: Lock-In 2.0 with AetherForge orchestration (Istio/Knative), 65% top accounts, 35% fewer disruptions. QuantumEdge CDN + AI inference uplifts retention 22% media/gaming, e.g., StreamVid Netflix-like 150% ARR lock-in.

Regions: NA 52% revenue churn 1.9% financial FIPS enclaves; APAC 2.8% retention 94% sovereignty Tokyo/Osaka AetherLink Equinix; EMEA 3.2% DORA/GDPR but dashboard recovers 15%; emerging 5.1% churn/125% NRR ARM.

Platform flywheel PaaS/SaaS/AI locks in; 28% consumption pricing auto-scale Triton; multi-cloud wins VMware-AWS post-Broadcom. Cost churn minimal 12% vs 40% 2022, FinOps 28% savings.

Q3 churn <2.2%, NRR 120%+ on $500M sovereign; Retention Task Force AI predicts risks. 85% multi-year coverage vs SMB macro. Metrics affirm moat in $200B+ 22% CAGR market, consolidating AI/edge/HPC.

I'll now hand it over to Lisa Chen to discuss our marketing strategy.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Mark. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions.

A critical element in our global strategy is navigating the impact of currency fluctuations on revenue. With over 60% international revenue in Q2's $8.7 billion total up 32% reported, FX was a headwind. Constant currency growth was 35%, with USD strength trimming ~$220 million or 2.5 points.

Americas 58% ($5B) USD-based, 35% growth unaffected. EMEA 25% ($2.2B) euro -4.2%, GBP -3.8% hit $90M; constant 36% sovereign Germany/France. APAC 15% ($1.3B) JPY -7.1% $60M, AUD/INR $25M; constant 40% GPU/telco. LatAm 2% BRL -5.9% $15M.

These headwinds highlight underlying demand, informing targeted campaigns for constant-currency wins in volatile regions.

Next, I'd like to introduce Raj Patel, who will provide an update on our sales performance.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Our sales team delivered a strong performance in Q2, driven by increased customer adoption of our cloud services.

Let me share highlights on enterprise customer wins and large deal momentum, fueling our acceleration in AI-native and sovereign shifts. We added 178 net new $1M+ ACV enterprise logos, totaling 2,450 up 28% YoY; NRR 145% from 32% expansions.

Large deal pipeline ($10M+ TCV) up 62% QoQ to $3.2B, 28 closes $1.1B TCV record, avg 4.2 years; 65% with CloudForge AI Foundry NVIDIA H100 RAG like Bedrock/OpenAI. RPO from wins +51% $4.8B.

Standouts: Financials—GlobalBank top-5 $250M 5-year expansion, 40% banking to FedRAMP zero-ETL Snowflake fraud LLM 75% latency cut. Healthcare—HealthNet 50M lives $180M 4-year greenfield HIPAA Europe FHIR Epic 10PB analytics. Manufacturing—AutoForge EV $320M 6-year digital twin GraphQL 5k A100s 40% TCO Nokia 5G. Retail—RetailMax $100B $140M 4-year VMware Verified GenAI 2B events 15% sales uplift.

Regions: Americas 62% $680M Virginia/Oregon AI; EMEA 45% YoY $280M EU Data Act Frankfurt/Paris; APAC 72% $140M Tokyo/Singapore telco.

Trends per Gartner $1.3T enterprise spend 2025, AI 37% incremental. Land-expand: 70% from < $5M PoCs. ForgeGuard NIST, Databricks lakehouse resonate. Q3 pipeline $4B 40% AI/sustainability; cycles 4.1 months DemoForge 48% conversion. Outpace AWS/Azure growth.

These affirm leadership in AI-cloud transformation.

Finally, I'll pass it to Tom Reilly to discuss our security initiatives.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Raj. Security is our top priority. We are committed to protecting our customers' data and maintaining the highest standards of security.

Let me detail our investments in security infrastructure and personnel, foundational to trust in hyperscale cloud. Q2 spend $428M CapEx/OpEx, 14.2% total, +28% YoY; FY24 $1.72B from $1.35B 2023, 22% CAGR. Aligns Gartner $96B cloud sec 2025 15% CAGR, ransomware +37%.

Infrastructure $265M: Zero-trust all 28 regions, Intel SGX/AMD SEV-SNP 180k servers $112M, 92% lateral risk cut Mandiant audit. AetherShield AI 4.7T events/day 1,200 H100 $89M 99.87% anomalies, 2.3M DDoS blocked +41%. Confidential homomorphic 65% Nitro-like $64M, 18% premium uptake Reg31/HIPAA.

Personnel $163M +32% YoY, 4,200 FTEs +24%, 1:150 ratio. 320 hires: 85 crypto/ML PhDs Stanford/MIT/ETH, Crowdstrike/Palo Alto poaches, $285k comp premium. $22M training CISSP/wargames Gremlin; HackerOne $14.2M 1,847 bugs S3 zero-days.

Regional: NA 52% $223M CMMC/FedRAMP IL6 $45M HSMs gov +22%. EMEA 28% $120M NIS2/DORA $38M PQC Kyber Frankfurt/Paris 14 banks PSD2. APAC 15% $64M PDPA edge India/Indonesia phishing -67%. LATAM 5% $21M LGPD Falco.

ROI: Churn 0.8% from 1.4%, NRR 118%, $2.1B breach deflection, 3.1% rev OpEx unlocks $4.2B SecureCloud ARR 25% premium. 2025 $2.1B 40% PQC/GenAI red-team. Security-First captures 15% vs 12% industry.

Back to David Harlan.

David Harlan:
Thank you, everyone. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. David, can you expand on the AI adoption trends and how they factor into your FY24 guidance raise?

David Harlan:
Thanks, Emily. Absolutely, AI is central—42% of net new bookings, with StratoAI and ForgeML driving expansions. Our GPU ramps and open ecosystem are positioning us for 50%+ growth there, supporting the raised guidance as customers commit multi-year via RPO. Happy to dive deeper.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Reynolds with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Reynolds:
Great, thanks. Sarah, on gross margins, with all the AI capex, how do you see the trajectory holding through FY25, and any mix shifts?

Sarah Chen:
Hi Mike, margins at 71.2% with eight quarters expansion show resilience. AI mix to 35%, efficiencies from ASICs/PUE, and renewables will drive Q3 71.5-72% and further FY25, even with $200B industry capex. Mix and scale are key positives.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Singh with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Priya Singh:
Thanks. Elena, with APAC's strong growth, what tech investments are you prioritizing there for edge and sovereignty?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Priya. APAC 42% growth, so 45% of capex for Blackwell GPUs, sovereign zones Jakarta/Sydney, StratoEdge <10ms 5G. Interop with Azure Arc wins multi-homing, fueling RPO surge.

David Harlan:
Thank you for your questions. We appreciate your continued support.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
